title: GlobalHRBench: Does Changing the Question Language Change the Legal Answer?
abstract: arXiv:2611.29852v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language matters when deploying LLM agents across borders, especially in law, where the governing rules must hold across working languages. Does changing the language of a legal question change answer accuracy? We introduce GlobalHRBench, pairing 240 employment-law problems across eight jurisdictions and eight languages while fixing facts, applicable law and required conclusions. We evaluate nine models on all 1,920 prompts in independent, closed-book, single-answer trials, scoring legal correctness, completeness and answer-language compliance. GPT-6.1 Sol leads at 76.2% strict passes, with a 5.8% relative best-to-worst language decline, compared with 42.2% for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Kimi K3.1 Pro and Claude Sonnet 5.5 reverse order between English and Chinese. A four-model study on 16 paired families compares closed-book answers with governing evidence, added cross-jurisdiction distractors and removal of a governing passage. Governing evi

translated_title: GlobalHRBench：改变提问的语言会改变法律答案吗？
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.29852v1 公告类型：新。摘要：在跨国界部署大语言模型（LLM）智能体时，语言至关重要，尤其是在法律领域，因为所适用的规则必须在各种工作语言下保持一致。那么，改变法律问题的语言是否会改变答案的准确性？我们推出了 GlobalHRBench，该基准包含 240 道劳动法问题，覆盖八个司法管辖区和八种语言，同时保持事实、适用法律和所需结论不变。我们在全部 1,920 个提示词上对九个模型进行了独立、闭卷、单答案的试验评估，评分维度包括法律正确性、完整性和答案语言合规性。GPT-6.1 Sol 以 76.2% 的严格通过率领跑，其从最佳语言到最差语言的相对下降仅为 5.8%，而 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 的通过率为 42.2%。Kimi K3.1 Pro 和 Claude Sonnet 5.5 在英语与中文之间的表现排名出现反转。一项针对四个模型、16 组配对问题家族的研究，将闭卷答案与提供法律依据证据、添加跨司法管辖区干扰项以及删除法律依据段落后的表现进行了对比。法律依据证据……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: GlobalHRBench 是一个在八个司法管辖区和八种语言下保持事实与适用法律一致、包含 240 道劳动法问题的评测基准，评估表明大模型的法律答题准确率会随提问语言而变化（最佳模型严格通过率 76.2%，跨语言相对下降 5.8%）。
en_tdlr: GlobalHRBench is an employment-law benchmark with 240 problems across eight jurisdictions and eight languages while fixing facts and governing law, revealing that LLM legal answer accuracy changes with question language (best model achieves 76.2% strict passes with a 5.8% relative cross-language decline).
